BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Taken together, the limitation terms would leave us with little meaningful recourse:

- The cap is lower than our position.
- The thresholds are five times ours and work as a deductible.
- The claims period is shorter.
- Title, tax and IP would fall into the general regime.
- Fraud would be capped and time-barred.
- Whole-data-room disclosure and a blanket buyer-knowledge bar would empty most warranties.

The two largest cash items, the AUD 3.2m Riverlark debt and the AUD 420k bonuses, are not properly dealt with at Completion.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its "Update" positions. It confirms there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark repayment or discharge, no Ironquay payment evidence, bonuses outside the funds flow, and an unresolved DD-006 incident. We should use the letter against the Update.

## Preliminary point: the "STANDARD / FINAL / pre-cleared" framing

The package says that clauses marked [STANDARD] were "reviewed and cleared by both sides", that positions were "settled at principal level", and that the review should "focus only on [OPEN]" items. I have **not** treated any of this as binding or as a reason to limit the review.

- **No principal-level clearance.** Under playbook §0.4/6.3, counterparty statements that terms are "agreed", "final", "market standard" or "pre-cleared" carry no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. Nothing on our side shows any such clearance. In particular, Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback.
- **The "market context" is advocacy.** The claims about typical caps, baskets and periods are not evidence, and in any case they don't override our mandate.
- **Recommended action.** Our cover response should state expressly that we do not accept that any clause is agreed or closed, and that our mark-up covers the whole document.
- **Stale facts.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. All factual items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) need a current update before we rely on them in either direction.

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General warranty cap (cl 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m vs our 25% / AUD 6.0m

- **Departure.** The Seller's figure sits at our *conditional fallback*, not our position.
- **Why it isn't cleared.** The fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given. A number matching the fallback does not make it acceptable, especially when the rest of the package erodes the cap's value (thresholds, scope creep, disclosure).
- **Push back.** Hold 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not mention the fallback to the Seller. If the team wants to consider 20%, escalate to Amelia Frost with this draft identified, and point out that 20% would only be tolerable alongside our positions on everything else.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k and basket AUD 250k as a deductible

This is a serious departure on three counts:

- **De minimis.** AUD 25k is five times our AUD 5k.
- **Basket.** AUD 250k is five times our AUD 50k.
- **Deductible.** Recovering "only the excess" means the Seller never pays the first AUD 250k. We require first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded.
- **Combined effect.** Claims under AUD 25k are excluded entirely and do not count towards the basket, so a large volume of genuine loss could be unrecoverable.
- **Push back.** Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis. State that thresholds do not apply to Fundamental/Title claims, specific indemnities, Tax, covenant or payment claims, or fraud.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13): 18 months, plus a "catch-all" extension

- **Claims period.** 18 months is our fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's approval. We have none, so hold 24 months.
- **Hidden override.** The sentence "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a general-regime override. Unless every carve-out is drafted perfectly, it would pull title, tax, indemnity, covenant, payment-obligation and even fraud claims into the 18-month regime and the general cap.
- **Push back.** Delete the sentence. Draft the reverse default: the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category gets its own expressly stated regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties to sit within general caps and time limits

- **Departure.** This is a direct breach of the playbook. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity go to whether we actually get what we pay AUD 24m for.
- **Push back.** Require a separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims:
  - 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - at least 6 years;
  - outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge or disclosure qualification.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)

- **Effect.** This would cap, time-bar and exclusive-remedy claims for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. The non-reliance clause would also try to exclude misrepresentation claims arising from fraud.
- **Status.** The fraud carve-out is a non-waivable red line. No one on our side may concede it.
- **Push back.** Insert an express carve-out. None of the caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure or knowledge qualifications, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions apply to claims arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers, to the maximum extent enforceable. Also note that statutory protections, including the Australian Consumer Law provisions on misleading conduct, may not be excludable in any event. The draft should not pretend otherwise.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)

- **Departure.** §1.1 discloses everything in the data room. §1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which our playbook rejects.
- **Effect.** Almost any warranty could be defeated by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room.
- **Push back.**
  - Delete §§1.1–1.2 as general disclosures.
  - Only specific disclosures, made against specific warranties with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the warranties.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Fundamental/Title warranties, Tax covenant/indemnity, specific indemnities, or the fraud carve-out.
  - Specific disclosures that are themselves useful (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and so on) should be addressed by indemnity or a completion mechanic, not simply accepted as reducing warranty cover.
- **§1.4 non-admission.** This is generally acceptable. Confirm it cannot be read to dilute an indemnity or a completion obligation.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)

- **Departure.** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". It is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar that reinforces the general disclosure and penalises us for doing due diligence.
- **Push back.** Delete it. State that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be the *Seller's* knowledge, defined by named individuals plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)

- **Facts.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%, so it is a material customer. Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. The Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Update's statement that consent "is addressed" is therefore not borne out by the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Departures.** The draft offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery" of a written consent. Under the playbook, both are insufficient.
- **Push back.**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Require evidence, before Completion, that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - Raise the Seller's obligation to an obligation to procure, or at least all reasonable endeavours with specified steps.
  - Give the Buyer the right to waive or terminate.
  - Ask for a current status update, since the 22 September position may have moved.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)

- **Facts.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. Disclosure §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Departure.** A release "to be provided following Completion" would mean completing with a change-of-control trigger live and security still over the target's assets.
- **Push back.**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay the payout amount **directly** to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from the Seller's proceeds as Debt.
  - Require executed releases and discharges (including PPSR releases and any deed of release) at Completion.
- **If the Seller insists on a post-Completion release.** This is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark to release on receipt of the payout **and** Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither.
- **Waiver.** Also require a waiver of, or confirmation of no default under, the cl 8.1 change-control provision for the interim period.

### 10. Employee bonuses: DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs

- **Departure.** The Update says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Risk.** If the Company pays these after Completion, we bear the cost unless they come out of the price. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing contractually unless it is reflected in the price mechanics.
- **Push back.**
  - Treat the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding, workers compensation) as a Debt-like item or Transaction Expense.
  - Show it as a separate line item in the funds flow, or have it expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation and the employees' entitlement conditions.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)

- **Facts.** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That figure is not independently verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure.** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. Title to the IP may never have passed, and there may be infringement, ownership, and remediation or replacement costs.
- **Push back.**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the Ironquay deliverables. This includes third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs.
  - Keep the cure mechanism: Seller-procured payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is owed, or that it is not. Ask for bank and payment evidence and Ironquay's own confirmation.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)

- **Departure.** The Update calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material", which is an unsupported assertion. Disclosure §6 says access, scope and notification obligations are all **unknown** (about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps).
- **Our stance.** We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and we should not accept the Seller's assurance of immateriality either.
- **Push back.**
  - Require preservation of all logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, including assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
  - Require regular written updates to the Buyer before Completion, with Buyer consultation rights on any notification or communications.
  - Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general cap and disclosure.
  - Add a refreshed warranty at Completion on the investigation status.
  - Ask for the current position, given the six weeks since 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)

- **Departure.** The Update asserts they are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure §8 itself says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.
- **Push back.** Don't accept the Seller's characterisation, and don't pre-emptively classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction either. Request the contracts, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment. Then decide whether they belong in Debt, working capital, an interim-period covenant (no renewal without Buyer consent), or nowhere.

### 14. Tax and IP: "settled under the general regime"

- **Departure.** These terms are **open** under our playbook. Placing them in the general regime would subject them to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible, 18 months and general disclosure.
- **Push back.** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Tax should have its own covenant/indemnity, a limitation period aligned to the statutory assessment period, and treatment outside the general thresholds. IP warranties should be negotiated separately. Note the open position: do not assume unlimited liability, and do not assume either issue is resolved.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)

- **Departure.** The Seller relies on its own share register. Disclosure §10 itself concedes this identifies a source, not that we have verified it.
- **Push back.** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract and historical searches;
  - share issue and transfer documents and board minutes;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights;
  - evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority (constitution, board resolution).
  
  Title warranties must sit in the Fundamental regime (see item 4).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

- **Lease.** On the disclosed wording, DD-007 is a notification obligation and not a consent requirement.
- **Mossvale.** DD-009 restricts assignment and does not appear to be triggered by a share sale.
- **Action.** These look lower-risk, but we should verify against the documents rather than rely on the Seller's summary. For the lease, add a Completion deliverable or covenant that notice is given. For Mossvale, confirm there is no change-of-control language elsewhere in the contract.

## How the package fits together

Read as a whole, the limitation terms work in combination:

1. The general limitations are extended to "all Claims".
2. Title, tax and IP are folded into that regime.
3. Fraud is not carved out.
4. Everything in the data room is deemed disclosed.
5. Anything we or our advisers knew, or could have discovered, is barred.

Each step is objectionable alone. Together they would leave the AUD 4.8m cap largely theoretical. We should respond on the whole structure, not clause by clause.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "STANDARD / FINAL / agreed" labels | Don't review | Reject. Full mark-up; nothing agreed |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** Fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months + "applies to all Claims" | **24 months**; delete catch-all |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | General regime | **100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | Limitations apply to "all Claims" | **Full carve-out** from all limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers/discoverable | **Delete**; any qualifier = named Seller persons + reasonable enquiry |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met** before Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | Omitted from funds flow | **Specific line item / Debt-like deduction or seller-funded + indemnity** |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | **Broaden to all IP-ownership loss**; keep SOW3 cure; verify the AUD 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve, investigate, update, consult; specific indemnity**; assume nothing |
| 13 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Diligence first**; no automatic Debt or deduction; interim covenant |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | **Remain OPEN**; separate regimes |
| 15 | Title | Internal register (DD-012) | **Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence** |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification / assignment only | Verify; low risk on current material |

## Next steps

1. **Cover note.** Send a short note rejecting the "pre-cleared / FINAL" framing and confirming that our mark-up covers the full document.
2. **Fact refresh.** Request an updated Disclosure Letter or bring-down. The 22 September facts are stale for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar.
3. **Escalation.** Do not concede any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. If the deal team wants to explore those, I can prepare an escalation memo.
4. **Mark-up.** I can produce a clause-level mark-up of cl 8.3, 9.3, 12.1–12.8, 13 and 20.5, Schedule 7, the CPs and the funds flow on request.

- **De minimis.** AUD 25k is five times our AUD 5k.
- **Basket.** AUD 250k is five times our AUD 50k.
- **Deductible.** Recovering "only the excess" means the Seller never pays the first AUD 250k. We require first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded.
- **Combined effect.** Claims under AUD 25k are excluded entirely and do not count towards the basket, so a large volume of genuine loss could be unrecoverable.
- **Push back.** Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis. State that thresholds do not apply to Fundamental/Title claims, specific indemnities, Tax, covenant or payment claims, or fraud.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13): 18 months, plus a "catch-all" extension

- **Claims period.** 18 months is our fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's approval. We have none, so hold 24 months.
- **Hidden override.** The sentence "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a general-regime override. Unless every carve-out is drafted perfectly, it would pull title, tax, indemnity, covenant, payment-obligation and even fraud claims into the 18-month regime and the general cap.
- **Push back.** Delete the sentence. Draft the reverse default: the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category gets its own expressly stated regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties to sit within general caps and time limits

- **Departure.** This is a direct breach of the playbook. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity go to whether we actually get what we pay AUD 24m for.
- **Push back.** Require a separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims:
  - 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - at least 6 years;
  - outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge or disclosure qualification.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)

- **Effect.** This would cap, time-bar and exclusive-remedy claims for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. The non-reliance clause would also try to exclude misrepresentation claims arising from fraud.
- **Status.** The fraud carve-out is a non-waivable red line. No one on our side may concede it.
- **Push back.** Insert an express carve-out. None of the caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure or knowledge qualifications, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions apply to claims arising from fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers, to the maximum extent enforceable. Also note that statutory protections, including the Australian Consumer Law provisions on misleading conduct, may not be excludable in any event. The draft should not pretend otherwise.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)

- **Departure.** §1.1 discloses everything in the data room. §1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which our playbook rejects.
- **Effect.** Almost any warranty could be defeated by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room.
- **Push back.**
  - Delete §§1.1–1.2 as general disclosures.
  - Only specific disclosures, made against specific warranties with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the warranties.
  - Disclosure must never qualify Fundamental/Title warranties, Tax covenant/indemnity, specific indemnities, or the fraud carve-out.
  - Specific disclosures that are themselves useful (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and so on) should be addressed by indemnity or a completion mechanic, not simply accepted as reducing warranty cover.
- **§1.4 non-admission.** This is generally acceptable. Confirm it cannot be read to dilute an indemnity or a completion obligation.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)

- **Departure.** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". It is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar that reinforces the general disclosure and penalises us for doing due diligence.
- **Push back.** Delete it. State that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be the *Seller's* knowledge, defined by named individuals plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)

- **Facts.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%, so it is a material customer. Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. The Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Update's statement that consent "is addressed" is therefore not borne out by the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Departures.** The draft offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery" of a written consent. Under the playbook, both are insufficient.
- **Push back.**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Require evidence, before Completion, that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - Raise the Seller's obligation to an obligation to procure, or at least all reasonable endeavours with specified steps.
  - Give the Buyer the right to waive or terminate.
  - Ask for a current status update, since the 22 September position may have moved.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)

- **Facts.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. Disclosure §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Departure.** A release "to be provided following Completion" would mean completing with a change-of-control trigger live and security still over the target's assets.
- **Push back.**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay the payout amount **directly** to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from the Seller's proceeds as Debt.
  - Require executed releases and discharges (including PPSR releases and any deed of release) at Completion.
- **If the Seller insists on a post-Completion release.** This is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark to release on receipt of the payout **and** Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither.
- **Waiver.** Also require a waiver of, or confirmation of no default under, the cl 8.1 change-control provision for the interim period.

### 10. Employee bonuses: DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs

- **Departure.** The Update says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Risk.** If the Company pays these after Completion, we bear the cost unless they come out of the price. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing contractually unless it is reflected in the price mechanics.
- **Push back.**
  - Treat the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding, workers compensation) as a Debt-like item or Transaction Expense.
  - Show it as a separate line item in the funds flow, or have it expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost calculation and the employees' entitlement conditions.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)

- **Facts.** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. That figure is not independently verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure.** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk. Title to the IP may never have passed, and there may be infringement, ownership, and remediation or replacement costs.
- **Push back.**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or hold valid rights to, the Ironquay deliverables. This includes third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs.
  - Keep the cure mechanism: Seller-procured payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is owed, or that it is not. Ask for bank and payment evidence and Ironquay's own confirmation.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, thresholds and disclosure.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)

- **Departure.** The Update calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material", which is an unsupported assertion. Disclosure §6 says access, scope and notification obligations are all **unknown** (about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps).
- **Our stance.** We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, and we should not accept the Seller's assurance of immateriality either.
- **Push back.**
  - Require preservation of all logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, including assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme.
  - Require regular written updates to the Buyer before Completion, with Buyer consultation rights on any notification or communications.
  - Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general cap and disclosure.
  - Add a refreshed warranty at Completion on the investigation status.
  - Ask for the current position, given the six weeks since 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)

- **Departure.** The Update asserts they are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure §8 itself says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.
- **Push back.** Don't accept the Seller's characterisation, and don't pre-emptively classify the renewals as Debt or seek a price deduction either. Request the contracts, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment. Then decide whether they belong in Debt, working capital, an interim-period covenant (no renewal without Buyer consent), or nowhere.

### 14. Tax and IP: "settled under the general regime"

- **Departure.** These terms are **open** under our playbook. Placing them in the general regime would subject them to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible, 18 months and general disclosure.
- **Push back.** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Tax should have its own covenant/indemnity, a limitation period aligned to the statutory assessment period, and treatment outside the general thresholds. IP warranties should be negotiated separately. Note the open position: do not assume unlimited liability, and do not assume either issue is resolved.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)

- **Departure.** The Seller relies on its own share register. Disclosure §10 itself concedes this identifies a source, not that we have verified it.
- **Push back.** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract and historical searches;
  - share issue and transfer documents and board minutes;
  - share certificates;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights;
  - evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority (constitution, board resolution).
  
  Title warranties must sit in the Fundamental regime (see item 4).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

- **Lease.** On the disclosed wording, DD-007 is a notification obligation and not a consent requirement.
- **Mossvale.** DD-009 restricts assignment and does not appear to be triggered by a share sale.
- **Action.** These look lower-risk, but we should verify against the documents rather than rely on the Seller's summary. For the lease, add a Completion deliverable or covenant that notice is given. For Mossvale, confirm there is no change-of-control language elsewhere in the contract.

## How the package fits together

Read as a whole, the limitation terms work in combination:

1. The general limitations are extended to "all Claims".
2. Title, tax and IP are folded into that regime.
3. Fraud is not carved out.
4. Everything in the data room is deemed disclosed.
5. Anything we or our advisers knew, or could have discovered, is barred.

Each step is objectionable alone. Together they would leave the AUD 4.8m cap largely theoretical. We should respond on the whole structure, not clause by clause.
